title: Learner 01 | Day 079: Probability, similarity, and numeric stability
body:
## Goal

Implement cosine similarity with a zero-vector policy and stable softmax using maximum subtraction.

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/experience/workflows/document_features.py`

**Method/unit:** `run_score_normalization`

**Why here:** This coordinates ordered steps and resource lifetime: orchestration calls the agreed operations/adapters and handles progress/cleanup without copying their rules.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Identical nonzero vectors have cosine 1; orthogonal vectors 0; large logits do not overflow.

**Boundaries:** Compose accepted collaborators once; delegate rules, storage and display.

## Research hints

1. Research **Probability, similarity, and numeric stability**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:docs.scipy.org Probability similarity and numeric stability`; use [SciPy statistics](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/tutorial/stats.html) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** Why should durable data live outside an application's disposable container layer?

**Review with @bitsnbyt3s:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
